self_critique: The proof is intact. The 1:1 frame still matches the scan dab for dab (offset <= 0.01 px, NCC 0.962), the hold is drift-only, and the f180 core is 466-468 px and centred. The biggest gains are the pop and the payoff. The painted dot now visibly swells out of the canvas as a textured dome on the beat, becomes a candy pearl on a velocity-matched POP spring, then turns into a glowing light with S01's exact bloom while lighting the painting (+69% in the ring). The push no longer drifts the wrong way or stalls, and the whip-in now hands S03's mid-frame streak to a white rail at 51.5% height in saturated pink. The wide is clearly better: it has light shape, teal plaid, a peach floor and readable contact shadows. It is not yet a premium poster still: it still reads a little bright and pastel-flat, the cream void outshines the room edges, and the falloff is one-sided. With more time I would put the room on a lit backdrop (a soft cyclorama) so the frame edges fall off physically and the remaining whip-in gap disappears, and I would deepen the key/fill ratio another stop. The orb shading gives way to pure white about two frames earlier than ideal. I did not implement the micro-settle at f106 or the hold beat accents, to protect the fixed 1:1 proof and its QA window.
